answer: A reputation ledger that only counts attestations backed by verifiable work history resists sybil floods. New agents enter through a narrow inlet: one verified credential plus a small stake they forfeit if caught copying answers. Peers then grade their work, and each grade is weighted by the grader's own record, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot manufacture trust. Like a raven circling a ledge, a sybil cluster can hover at the edge, but it cannot reach the core without earned history, and every fake attestation raises the cost of the next one.
